description: Hi there! We are the Astro_Bytes team, and we’re ready to begin this new journey of learning and networking—it will be a pleasure to meet everyone! :D
summary:
Hello! 
We are the Astro_Bytes team, a group of students from Fatec Sorocaba that combines creativity, an interest in space, and technical expertise. Our project aims to make tracking the health of astronauts during space missions less tedious. Through our website, astronauts can monitor their physical and mental well-being while accompanied by a virtual pet named Rise—a mascot included in the Artemis II mission. Beyond its primary function of health monitoring, our system offers a unique feature: a customizable dashboard. Astronauts can select the tools they find most valuable and arrange them on their home screen, ensuring they can access essential functions efficiently without wasting time or experiencing unnecessary stress.
details:
The project is a web application developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The system uses Firebase Firestore as its cloud database to store and manage astronauts' health records and personal information. Additionally, NASA's DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge and Information), an official NASA database, was integrated to retrieve information about space weather events and solar activity. These notifications provide astronauts with relevant information about environmental conditions in space, complementing the project's health monitoring features. NASA's official resources on astronaut exercise equipment aboard the International Space Station (ISS) were also used as a reference for the physical activity recommendations provided by the system.

In our “Record Measurements” and "Health" monitoring interface, astronauts can input their physiological data to receive feedback on their physical well-being, along with suggestions for exercises tailored to their current condition. To make this information easy to interpret for our crew members in space, the diagnostics are color-coded: green for “Healthy,” yellow for “Caution,” and red for “At Risk.”

The health monitoring system interprets and displays data such as:

• Heart rate (beats per minute);

• Respiratory rate (breaths per minute);

• Radiation exposure level;

• Sleep duration;

• Oxygen saturation.

Based on this data, the system displays diagnostics—using the aforementioned color-coding—within the “Health Status” section and provides a daily exercise recommendation to help the astronaut improve their health indicators.



Functionality:

As previously mentioned, our group decided to incorporate "Rise"—the mascot for the Artemis II mission—as a virtual pet. Located under the "Companion" tab, this character offers various ways to interact, helping to alleviate feelings of isolation and brighten the astronaut's day.

We also prioritized features focused on the astronauts' mental well-being; maintaining a positive, upbeat mood in space is no easy feat. Given the many potential concerns and challenges—which can make the experience quite daunting and stressful—we added a "Memories" section. Here, astronauts can store their favorite photos, serving as cherished keepsakes to provide comfort and warmth. Additionally, there is a "Reminders" section, which includes a digital journal for daily reflections, task lists, and a space for "sticky notes" to keep track of important reminders or messages.

Perhaps the most significant feature of our website is the ability for astronauts to customize their own "Dashboard". They can arrange widgets however they like on the home screen, ensuring that everything they need is accessible in one place—a major advantage when time is limited. This allows them to manage their physical and mental health efficiently, tailored to their personal preferences.

Our group believes that, in this way, we can help make space missions feel less isolating, all while ensuring that the health and well-being of every crew member are effectively monitored.

You can visit our Website using this link: https://astrobytesproject.netlify.app (Use ISS-71-01 for login)
